facts.title: The first of the family is in New Zealand by 1855
facts.body: Thomas Finch: last recorded in Sproughton, Suffolk in about 1823, in Howick, Auckland by 1855. The tree does not name a ship.

facts.title: 14 people are recorded on both sides of the world
facts.body: Each was recorded in Europe and later in New Zealand. The earliest is there by 1855, the latest by 1955. Many more must have made the voyage: these are the ones whose own records show both ends.

facts.title: Fanny Page Loveless ended 19,000 km from the start
facts.body: First recorded in Lambeth, London, last in Linwood, Christchurch. No one in the tree is recorded farther from where they began.

facts.title: James Finch is recorded in 5 places
facts.body: Sproughton, Suffolk, then Woodbridge, Suffolk, then Clopton, Suffolk, then Burgh, Suffolk, then Essex. More places than anyone else in the tree, counting a county or country only when no town inside it is named, which says as much about how well this life is recorded as about how far it went.

facts.title: 16 recorded births and baptisms in Norwich
facts.body: From 1654 to 1776. No other place has as many.

facts.title: 8 people are on the map only because a child was born
facts.body: 6 of them are women. No record of their own names a place: not a birth, a marriage or a burial. The only thing that says where they were is the entry for a child's birth or baptism.

facts.title: 14 went out to New Zealand. Nobody is recorded coming back
facts.body: 14 people are first recorded on one side of the world and last recorded in New Zealand. Not one person in the tree is first recorded in New Zealand and last recorded anywhere else. For this family the voyage was one way.

facts.title: One family was split by the voyage
facts.body: Brothers and sisters, one recorded in New Zealand and another, alive at the time, last recorded on the other side of the world. Of the children of Edward Finch and Susanna Scribner, Thomas is in New Zealand by 1855; Martha and James, still living then, are last recorded in Britain. Whether they met again, the tree does not say.

facts.title: Susan Mary Finch: 94 years with no record
facts.body: Recorded in Howick, Auckland in 1862, and not again until Auckland in 1956. It is the longest silence between two places in the tree. On the map the light waits where it was last seen, growing dim.

facts.title: The United States: first recorded in 1778
Ireland: first recorded in 1849
facts.body: Mary Clementina Brady was born there.

leads.title: Edwin Watkins and Fanny Page Loveless: both sides of the world in 1874
leads.body: Recorded in Lambeth, London and in Linwood, Christchurch in the same year. The voyage took two to three months, so it is possible, just. Worth checking both dates.

leads.title: The oldest move on the map is the one in doubt
leads.body: Francis Barlow: recorded as a child in Mucklestone, Staffordshire in 1639, a father in St Benedict, Norwich by 1654. 250 km, and he would have been about 15. The tree itself says: Mucklestone identity doubtful. If these are two men, this journey never happened.
